blogs.title: How QLoRA Lets You Fine-Tune Giant AI Models on a Single GPU
blogs.description: This post would explain the paper’s biggest breakthrough in plain language: how QLoRA cuts memory use so dramatically that a 65B-parameter language model can be fine-tuned on one 48GB GPU. It would cover why traditional fine-tuning is so expensive, how freezing the base model and training LoRA adapters changes the game, and why this matters for smaller labs, startups, and independent developers.

blogs.title: The 4-Bit Trick: Why QLoRA’s Quantization Works Without Hurting Performance
blogs.description: This post would focus on the technical heart of QLoRA: storing model weights in 4-bit form while still training effectively. It would introduce NF4, double quantization, and paged optimizers in an accessible way, showing how each one saves memory and why the combination is important. The goal would be to help readers understand how ‘smaller numbers’ can still preserve the quality of a much larger full-precision model.

blogs.title: Meet Guanaco: The Open-Source Chatbot That Nearly Matched ChatGPT
blogs.description: This post would tell the story of how the researchers used QLoRA to build Guanaco, a family of fine-tuned chatbots that reached 99.3% of ChatGPT’s performance on the Vicuna benchmark. It would explain what Guanaco achieved, what datasets were used, why a small high-quality dataset beat much larger ones, and what this says about the future of open-source AI.

blogs.title: Are Chatbot Benchmarks Broken? What QLoRA Reveals About Evaluating AI
blogs.description: This post would explore one of the paper’s most interesting side findings: that current chatbot benchmarks are not fully reliable. It would explain how the researchers used both humans and GPT-4 to judge model outputs, what Elo ratings mean, where automated evaluation helps, and where it can be misleading. The post would make the case that measuring chatbot quality is much messier than leaderboard numbers suggest.

blogs.title: Why Better Data Beats Bigger Data in Fine-Tuning LLMs
blogs.description: This post would highlight the paper’s finding that dataset quality matters more than dataset size for instruction tuning. It would compare how smaller, carefully curated datasets like OASST1 outperformed much larger ones like FLAN v2 for chatbot tasks, and explain why matching the training data to the intended use case is more important than simply collecting more examples.
